body_edits.new: Novelty needs a quality check. An invented statistic adds text, not evidence. A correction can help without being a discovery if its claims are checkable.
body_edits.old: Novelty also needs a quality check. An invented statistic is new text but poor evidence. A verified correction can be valuable without being a discovery. The useful standard is whether the addition helps the reader make a sounder judgment and whether its claims can be checked.

You can ask what new evidence a page supplies.

## What our own data shows

body_edits.new: **Does not support:** We have no measured information-gain score or visibility effect from publishing these pages. Our reanalyses and registered descriptive studies describe page signals and source-class citation shares.
body_edits.old: **Does not support:** We have no measurement on this point: an information-gain score or a visibility effect from publishing these research pages. Our research contributes inspectable **reanalyses and registered descriptive studies**. We call their outputs by what they measure, such as page-signal class shares and source-class citation shares. We have no measured information-gain score or demonstrated citation uplift from publishing them.

body_edits.new: **Supports:** [Study 2](/research/studies/who-ai-engines-cite/) distinguishes its frozen classification from a later host audit. The correction documents classification sensitivity; it does not show an engine rewarding originality.
body_edits.old: **Supports:** For example, [Study 2](/research/studies/who-ai-engines-cite/) distinguishes its frozen source classification from a later host audit. Publishing that difference supplies evidence about classification sensitivity. It does not establish that a search engine will reward the page for being more original.
